notes: Steps A-F complete. The open question - did the alkalinized ropivacaine remain free of visible precipitate - is answered 'partly', in two halves that point opposite ways. In vitro the answer is yes: the laboratory phase located the point at which a precipitate appeared, used a quantity below it, and reported no precipitate under an optical microscope over five minutes at room temperature. In tissue the answer is no: in the rat sub-study every solution recovered from the popliteal fossa five minutes after injection had precipitated, including the unmodified clinical-use preparation, and most of all the alkalinized ones. And the clinical phase never inspected the solutions given to patients at all - precipitation was a laboratory and animal observation throughout, while the trial's own endpoints were sensory and motor onset, block spread and duration. That scope difference is what sets the limit on this paper against D017, and it is the reverse of Milner 2000 (S-686-16, this paper companion in the same claim), a pure laboratory solution study whose only business was pH and precipitate. D017 goes confirmed -> refuted on the laboratory half of its own scope, with the five-minute window, the single strength, the Fulling 20-minute counter-finding and the rat result all named in the reason. D018 and C027 were re-judged and both stay narrowed. Step D: all 320 claims screened by keyword and the 24 plausible hits read; only D017, D018 and C027 are touched.
